chunk_findings.detail: `write` still claims it adds or replaces `name` inside the working tree, but the new call follows a symlink instead of replacing it. Given a temp repo at `/tmp/repo` and `escape` as a symlink to `/tmp/outside.txt`, `write("escape", "pwned")` used to atomically replace the symlink with a regular file under `/tmp/repo`; `fsio.replace_text` writes through the link, leaves `escape` as a symlink, and overwrites `/tmp/outside.txt`. The working tree git sees is unchanged, and content lands outside the fake repo. A mid-write crash also leaves a partial file where `atomic_write` did not.

chunk_findings.detail: `write` still documents adding or replacing the working-tree file at `name` and returning that path, but the new `fsio.replace_text` call is explicitly write-through: a symlink at `self.path / name` is followed instead of replaced. Given a helper path where `name` is a symlink to a file outside the temp repo, `write(name, "hello")` mutates that outside target, leaves the worktree entry a symlink, and a later commit records the link rather than the text. The previous `atomic_write` replaced the path in place, so this is a behavior change that breaks the method contract on that input.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_posix_file_lock_holds_an_advisory_lock` only asserts `lock.exists()` inside `P.DEFAULT.file_lock`. A `file_lock` that creates the path and yields without taking an advisory lock (`fcntl.flock` / `LOCK_EX` / `LOCK_NB`) still passes, so the test does not show a lock is held. A second overlapping `file_lock` on the same path would be the input that distinguishes a real hold from a touch.

chunk_findings.detail: `Windows._refuse` always appends the literal "(Windows)" while also interpolating `os.name`. On the supported hosts where this adapter is what the tests actually call (`os.name == "posix"`), `Windows().which("git")` raises `NotImplementedError("Platform.which is unavailable on posix (Windows)")`. The message names two different operating systems, so any check or log that treats the text as the host platform is wrong.
